examination_results.Oral Examination: Intraoral inspection reveals severe attrition with flattening and loss of cusp morphology on the occlusal and incisal surfaces of virtually all teeth. Multiple teeth exhibit dentin and localized enamel exposure, with the lower anterior teeth showing significant incisal edge shortening (mean incisal reduction: 3.5 mm). The estimated reduction in occlusal vertical dimension is approximately 5.8 mm, with a corresponding decrease in lower facial height. There is pronounced mobility in lower incisors (Miller Grade II-III) and upper first molars (Grade I-II), with visible anterior mandibular tooth displacement and mild malalignment. Generalized advanced gingivitis present: gingival margins are erythematous and edematous with bleeding on probing at more than 80% of sites. Periodontal pocket depths of 6–8 mm noted in lower anterior region and upper molars; clinical attachment loss averages 4.9 mm in affected sites. Alveolar bone hyperplasia is present with nodular protrusions palpable on the buccal aspect of the maxilla and mandible, especially in the premolar and molar regions. Masseter muscles visibly hypertrophic and tender bilaterally; muscle palpation elicits pain (reported VAS 6/10) in masseter and temporal regions. Notable tongue indentations along lateral margins. Masticatory muscles are tense, with reduced ability to relax post-examination. Salivary flow appears mildly reduced. Several teeth demonstrate thermal hypersensitivity on percussion and cold testing. One porcelain crown on upper left first molar shows chipping and marginal leakage. Temporomandibular joint exam reveals moderate pain (VAS 5/10) with repetitive clicking during opening and closing, but maximal opening amplitude is preserved at 42 mm.
examination_results.Auxiliary Examination: Wireless intraoral sensor records upper and lower dental contact for a total of 121.6 minutes over a standard 7-hour sleep observation (normal: <20 minutes), with high-frequency intermittent episodes of sustained contact each lasting 5–70 seconds. Electromyography of facial muscles demonstrates maximum bilateral masseter clenching potentials averaging 418 µV (normal: 170–200 µV) and temporal muscle potentials averaging 165 µV (normal: <85 µV), with prolonged contraction bursts. The mean hourly incidence of rhythmic masticatory muscle activity (RMMA) during sleep is measured at 35 episodes/hour (reference: <5/hour), with clustering during non-REM stages N1–N2. Multichannel polysomnography reveals reduced slow-wave sleep (N3: 6% of total sleep time, reference: >13%), frequent micro-arousals preceding masticatory muscle activity, and mean heart rate elevations of 11 bpm above baseline during RMMA clusters. Lateral cephalometric radiography and panoramic imaging show severe vertical loss of dental height in the anterior mandibular segment, alveolar bone nodular protrusions, irregular crestal bone margins, and mild condylar flattening and subchondral sclerosis of the temporomandibular joints. MRI demonstrates thickening of the right and left masseter muscles (measured cross-sectional area: R 6.2 cm², L 6.5 cm²; normal: 3–4 cm²) with no acute internal derangement of the joint identified. No neoplastic or acute osseous lesions observed.
